transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has completed his trip to China.
He ended by holding a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese
President Xi Jinping.
NPR's Jennifer Pax says Trump wanted to emphasize a point.
For Trump, he wanted to talk about nuclear arms control.
At the start of the trilateral meeting, he said the three of them are making history,
but they are uniquely placed to reduce the number of nuclear weapons, something that
Beijing has not been keen on in the past, given that it has the smallest stockpile of
nuclear arsenals of the three.
And China thinks it's unfair.
It has to be at the table at all.
Putin would like to talk about an end to Russia's war in Ukraine, but on Moscow's terms.
But the complexity of these issues means it's really hard to see anything substantive coming
out of this.
NPR's Jennifer Pax reporting from Shenzhen, China.
The two other leaders at the summit expressed their views.
Chinese President Xi, speaking through an interpreter, hailed the historic nature of
the meeting before it began.
This is the first ever meeting between the top leaders of our three countries in history.
It is indeed a groundbreaking move.
We will be having discussions on the theme of upholding world peace and promoting strategic
stability in major country relations.
And Russian President Putin worked to bring the conversation around to Ukraine.
He also spoke through an interpreter.
Our countries have numerous shared interests in the settlement of regional conflicts, including
obviously the conflict in Ukraine.
We discussed this yesterday with the president of China.
And today, at the initiative of the president of the United States of America, we focused
on that during our bilateral meeting.
Before the trilateral meeting started, Ukrainian officials announced they'd again attack
the key bridge between Russia and the annexed Crimean Peninsula.
It's a key route for Russia to move personnel and materiel to the battlefront with Ukraine.
In Gaza, there is only one crossing open where aid and commercial goods can enter.
It's controlled by Israel.
Israel's facing growing international pressure to allow winter essentials into the region.
Ukraine peers Anas Baba has more.
Under the terms of the ceasefire, for the past 13 months, Israel was supposed to allow
600 trucks of supplies into Gaza every day.
But for about a year, the daily average has been closer to 200 trucks.
Germany donated months ago a cargo scanner to be used at a second crossing at Aries in
northern Gaza and urged Israel to allow more aid in.
But Israeli authorities say Aries crossing will not be open for cargo.
This will be screened there and then escorted south to Karim Shalom, the only operational
crossing into Gaza, for further inspection.
Anas Baba, NPR News, Gaza City.
You're listening to NPR News from Washington.
The United Nations' highest court has found that Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
Muslims in its 2017 military operations.
The International Court of Justice says that Myanmar's security forces acted with genocidal
intent.
The court found around 10,000 Rohingya were violently killed.
The entire community was faced with targeted arsons, masks and public rapes, and the killings
of infants and children.
In the U.S., Democrats' new congressional majorities could mean some big education changes.
NPR's Corey Turner explains that includes student loans.
Speaking on Wednesday, Senator Bernie Sanders said federal student loan policy is "an absolute
priority" for him once Democrats retake control of Congress.
Specifically, he's pushing back on the strict new loan limits Republicans created for many
professional training programs, including in nursing and other health care-related jobs.
The idea that the Trump administration has provided disincentence for people to get into
professions that we desperately need through their student loan policy is absurd.
In the next Congress, Sanders is expected to lead the Senate committee that handles
education.
Corey Turner, NPR News.
Forecasters say significant storms in California and in Florida have led to flash flooding
watches and warnings.
Florida's Atlantic coast has gotten heavy rain, so as California's Pacific coast, there
are flood cautions from San Francisco to Los Angeles.
It's NPR.

topics.text: Trump completes China trip with trilateral nuclear arms meeting alongside Putin and Xi Jinping
Ukraine announces new attack plans on key Russia-Crimea bridge ahead of trilateral summit
Israel keeps Kerem Shalom as Gaza's only open aid crossing amid pressure to admit more aid
Germany-donated cargo scanner for Gaza's Kerem Shalom crossing remains undeployed as Israel refuses Erez crossing cargo
International Court of Justice finds Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya Muslims in 2017 operations
Sanders vows to prioritize federal student loan policy, challenging new loan limits on health professions training
Flash flood watches issued for Florida's Atlantic coast and California's Pacific coast from San Francisco to Los Angeles
